summary: The four verses of the Serug and Nahor entries are rendered accurately: verbs, binyanim, numbers and names all match the Hebrew, and the Onkelos rulings are correct. The unit has no normative anchors. The main fault is the sense of מֵאָה in 11:23 and 11:25, filled mechanically with `3` ('a hundredth part'), which does not fit a cardinal; both senses are removed and the reason given in the notes. One learner note in 11:22 overstates the rule for singular nouns after tens, and 11:25 gains a note on עֶשְׂרֵה.

patches.reason: Sense `3` of מֵאָה is 'a hundredth part' (the ordinal/fractional use), not the cardinal 'two hundred'. The pack lists no fitting sense, so the sense is removed.

patches.value: dual form מָאתַיִם: 'two hundred'. No sense is given: the only sense the pack lists under מֵאָה is `3`, 'a hundredth part', which does not fit; the entry's head meaning 'hundred' is the one meant.
patches.reason: Records why the sense was removed, as the brief requires.

value: וַיְחִי and וַיּוֹלֶד are wayyiqtols that carry the genealogy forward.
The etnaḥta on שָׁנָה divides the verse: age, then the birth.

The noun שָׁנָה stays singular after שְׁלֹשִׁים. A few nouns that are often counted, such as שָׁנָה 'year', יוֹם 'day' and אִישׁ 'man', are usually singular after the tens; most other nouns take the plural.
patches.reason: The note said the singular follows 'tens in general'; it is the rule only for a group of frequently counted nouns, so the learner note as written is not true.

patches.value: עֶשְׂרֵה is the form of 'ten' used in eleven to nineteen with a feminine noun; after תְּשַׁע it makes 'nineteen'.
patches.reason: The gloss 'teen' needs a note for a learner: the lexicon gives עָשָׂר as 'ten', and the compound form is otherwise unexplained.
